codingse: Project 2020 SEEL thesis: 4 regions, 4 investors, and 8 goods. mu is retained because the thesis does not specify this implementation's mutation-rate parameter.
ga: Project 2023 thesis, Section 4.1: population=30, crossover=0.8, mutation=0.1. Mutation follows the thesis code (Algorithm/GA.py Mutation + Combine/JGA.py Transition): each offspring mutates with probability 0.1 and redraws one uniformly chosen gene from its own domain (the value may stay the same).
sa_sets: Project 2023 thesis: 8 searchers, 4 regions, 2 goods per region; mu is retained from the existing SA-SETS implementation. SensorEncodingV3 uses V2 coverage selection and redundancy removal, but a routing-rejected sensor remains scheduled with next_hop=-1 and the chromosome is not modified.
ring_se: Goods are a single shared pool (no per-region partition), while every searcher-good pair draws one of h ring segments uniformly at random (per-pair since 2026-10-13; per-searcher before, lifetime within noise) to constrain that trade's sensor-pair crossover/mutation span (80% within-segment, 20% segment-plus-adjacent-fragment). Crossover retains both role-preserving children: child1 elitistically updates only its searcher, and each good is always replaced by its best visitor child2 even when worse (EN acceptance since 2026-10-12; EE before).
ring_sepri: Same market, regions and operators as ring_se; only the chromosome changes to PriorityEncoding (energy-only activation order + energy-plus-farness routing order, 2N priority genes). Sensing levels are chosen greedily by the decoder.
sets: Project SETS experiment setting: 8 searchers, 4 regions, 2 goods per region, and mutation rate 0.4.
si_sets: Selective-Investment SETS (formerly SI_SETSv2): each searcher trades only with the goods of its selected region; identity-sensor regions, initialization, crossover and mutation are shared with SA-SETS. RL-SETSv4 market-update ablation without reinforcement learning. Every searcher-good pair produces two crossover children and mutates each with probability mu. Searchers accept only their best improving child1; every visited good accepts the best visiting child2 only when it improves the old good.
linucb_ring_se: Ring_SE (SensorEncoding, w=8) where every searcher-good pair picks its own segment with a shared LinUCB model. One span per segment is drawn with the original 80/20 rule; features describe what each span exchanges (effective differences in {1-2, 3-4, >=5}, inactive differences, span length, active ratio, progress, progress x small difference). Reward 0.5[child1 improves searcher] + 0.5[child2 improves good]; the model persists across lifetime segments.
linucb_ring_sepri: Same per-pair LinUCB segment choice as linucb_ring_se on Ring_SEpri (PriorityEncoding).
qea: Global conditional-thermometer QEA adaptation; n=30 matches GA population. Rotation=0.01*pi, probability floor=0.01; exploratory defaults, not tuned. Matched controls share initialization, decoding, elite path and evaluation budget; classical update rate=0.05, random has no update. Han & Kim 2002 DOI:10.1109/TEVC.2002.804320.
qts: Quantum-inspired Tabu Search (Chiang et al. 2014) on conditional-thermometer Q-bits (5 gates per sensing level, 9 per priority rank). Update toward iteration best except tabu gates where best and worst agree; probability floor=0.01; init=uniform gives equal option probabilities. n=30, rotation=0.05*pi: best iteration-best setting of the 2026-10-18 grid (n in {10,30} x rotation 0.01-0.15*pi, MAP01-06 seed 7-11, budget 10000), tuned on the same maps as the reported results.
qdit_ts: QTS loop (Chiang et al. 2014) on multi-state Q-dits: one amplitude per option (6 per sensing level, 10 per priority rank, 1600 for 100 sensors), uniform prior 1/sqrt(d). Per gene, best==worst is tabu, otherwise a Givens rotation moves probability from the iteration-worst option to the iteration-best only, keeping the worst at probability floor=0.01; options unordered. n=30, rotation=0.2*pi: best setting of the 2026-10-18 grid (n in {10,30} x rotation 0.01-0.30*pi x iteration/global best, MAP01-06 seed 7-11, budget 10000); confirmed on seed 12-21.
ga_elitist: Same initialization, integer encoding, n=30, cu=0.8 and the 2023-thesis mutation (mu=0.1, one gene per mutated chromosome) as GA; carry 2 unmodified elites with cached fitness. Elite count is an exploratory, untuned default.
ga_adaptive: Srinivas and Patnaik (1994), DOI:10.1109/21.286385, equations (5)-(8): pair-specific crossover and individual-specific mutation from generation mean/max fitness; k1=k3=1, k2=k4=0.5, default mutation floor 0.005. Proportional selection uses a nonnegative shift for WSN fitness. The published binary chromosome is adapted to integer SensorEncoding with sensor-aligned two-point crossover and domain-valid mutation; this is not a replication of the original benchmark encoding.
pso: Exploratory sensor-encoded PSO baseline: 30 particles, inertia 0.7, cognitive/social coefficients 1.5, normalized velocity cap 0.2. Each normalized coordinate is discretized using its own SensorEncoding gene domain; all scores use the shared decoder and fitness service.
sa_setspri: Same market, identity-free regions and operators as sa_sets (n8 h4 w2 mu0.4, EN); only the chromosome changes to PriorityEncoding (2N priority genes, sensing levels chosen greedily by the decoder). Uniform random initialization (no CCS, the encoding has no level gene), no region alignment (no on/off gene), mutatev1 structure with values 0-9.
si_setspri: Same market as si_sets (n8 h4 w8 mu0.4, per-region goods pools, role-separated EN update); only the chromosome changes to PriorityEncoding. Uniform random initialization, no region alignment, mutatev1 structure with values 0-9.
sa_sets_target: SA-SETS market search with TargetCoding. Each target gene selects a coverage candidate and target priority; search regions split candidate choices of energy-critical targets.
qdit_ts_smooth: Qdit-TS register (amplitudes, 6 options per sensing level, 10 per priority rank, uniform prior). Per gene, best==worst is tabu, otherwise Givens rotations between every pair (i in kernel around best, j in kernel around worst) by rotation*g_i*l_j with g/l the kernel renormalized to 1, so the angles add up to rotation and kernel (1,) equals qdit_ts; floor 0.01, options at the floor left out of l. n=30, rotation=0.2*pi as qdit_ts; kernel (1, 0.25) was the best non-trivial kernel in the 2026-10-18 sweep (smoothing never beat kernel (1,)).
qts_pri: QTS (iteration-best rotation, tabu, floor 0.01, uniform prior) on PriorityEncoding: each sensor has an activation and a routing priority gene with 10 values, 9 thermometer gates each (1800 Q-bits for 100 sensors); sensing levels chosen greedily by the decoder (same chromosome as ring_sepri). n=30, rotation=0.08*pi: best iteration-best setting of the 2026-10-18 grid on MAP01-06 seed 7-11.
qdit_ts_pri: Qdit-TS (iteration-best Givens rotation, tabu, floor 0.01, uniform prior) on PriorityEncoding: one row of 10 amplitudes per activation / routing priority gene (2000 amplitudes for 100 sensors); sensing levels chosen greedily by the decoder (same chromosome as ring_sepri). n=10, rotation=0.03*pi: best setting of the 2026-10-18 grid (n in {10,30} x rotation 0.01-0.30*pi x iteration/global best, MAP01-06 seed 7-11); seed 12-21: 1164.3 vs ring_sepri 1158.9 (p=.11).
